s:

s: More than three-fourths of India's production of raw silk comes from –

the two States' combined share has fallen — now about 59% (2023-24) (app notes 4:83, sub 6).
Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh together gave over three-fourths of India's raw silk when asked (about 59% in 2023-24).

s:
Consider the following statements:
Assertion (A) : West Bengal is the leading producer of fish in India.
Reason (R) : West Bengal has well-developed fishing industry along the sea coast.
Select the correct answer from the code given below :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
x:
Andhra Pradesh is now the leading fish producer (about 30% of India's fish) — now A would be false (AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 p.74).
When asked, West Bengal was the leading fish producer (A true), but about 90% of its fish is inland, not from a sea-coast industry (R false).

s: Kerala stands first among rubber-growing states in India. What is its share in India's rubber production?
x: Kerala dominates natural rubber, giving about 90% of India's output (more than 90% when asked), followed by Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.
flag: Outdated: recent Rubber Board data put Kerala's share near 70-75%.

s: Which state produces the biggest cashewnut?
x:
Most books: Kerala (long the leading cashew state and processing hub; DCCD 2008-09 put Kerala ahead of Karnataka and Goa). Strictly: Maharashtra is the largest producer (182.79 thousand t in 2025-26, Lok Sabha reply) and is not offered.
Among the options, Kerala is the answer books give: it was long India's leading cashew producer and processor. Goa, Karnataka and Puducherry produced less.
flag: Outdated: Maharashtra is now the largest cashew producer (not offered).

s: Which of the following statements is NOT correct?
o: India is the largest producer of milk in the world
India is the biggest producer of vegetables in the world
India is the second largest producer of rice in the world
India is one of the largest producers of sugarcane
x:
India overtook China as the world's largest rice producer in 2024-25 — now statement 4 ("2nd in rice") is also wrong (PMF Environment 07 p.37).
India is 2nd, not 1st, in vegetables (China 1st), so statement 2 is the incorrect one; India is 1st in milk and among the top sugarcane producers. (Rice: India was 2nd when asked, now 1st.)
flag: Rice: India became world's largest producer in 2024-25, so statement 3 is now also false.

s: Next to Paddy, the principal food grain crop in Andhra Pradesh
x:
Most books and keys: jowar. Strictly, in residual AP maize now has more area and output than jowar (AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 p.46 lists maize among the major crops; area figures: general knowledge, not checked).
Jowar is the APPSC 2017 key: in the textbook (undivided AP) pattern it is the principal foodgrain after paddy.
flag: In residual AP maize now exceeds jowar in area/output; key reflects older textbook data.

s: What is the rank of Andhra Pradesh in milk production during 2018-19 as per reports of ministry of agriculture and farmers welfare, government of India?
src: APPSC Combined Recruitment (Hostel Welfare Officer, Division
x:
AP fell to 7th in milk in 2023-24 (139.94 lakh MT) — now 7th (AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 p.69).
In 2018-19 Andhra Pradesh was 4th in milk, after UP, Rajasthan and MP. It slipped to 7th in 2023-24.

s: At the present state of our knowledge and resource position, India will remain self-sufficient for the next three decades in –
x:
India is no longer self-sufficient in coking coal — now 2024-25 output 66.49 MT against imports of 57.07 MT (app notes 4:87 sub 3; PMF Human & Economic Geography 05 p.21)
The 1993 key was coking coal, then judged sufficient for three decades, while tin, copper and petroleum were import-dependent (now India imports about 57 MT of coking coal a year).

s: Sakkar Nagar is an important sugar producing centre of
x:
Nizamabad district went to Telangana on 2 June 2014 — now Sakkar Nagar is in Telangana (AP Reorganisation Act 2014)
Sakkar Nagar (Bodhan, Nizamabad) was in Andhra Pradesh when asked (2008); it is now in Telangana (now Telangana).

s: In Andhra Pradesh, the Kesoram Cements is located in the district of:
x:
Karimnagar went to Telangana in 2014 and Basantnagar is now in Peddapalli district — now Kesoram's plant is in Telangana, not AP
Kesoram Cements' plant is at Basantnagar in Karimnagar district (now Peddapalli, Telangana) – in undivided AP when asked (2010).
flag: Karimnagar/Basantnagar is now in Telangana (Peddapalli); valid only for undivided AP.

s: Which country of the world is the largest producer and exporter of soft timber and wood pulp?
x:
FAO 2022 data — now USA is the largest pulp producer (23.5%), Brazil the largest pulp exporter (29%) and Russia the largest sawn-wood exporter (Canada 2nd) (PMF Part 5 p.91)
Canada was the largest producer and exporter of soft timber and wood pulp when asked (now the USA leads pulp production and Brazil pulp exports).

s: The Gatiman Express runs between
src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
x:
the Gatimaan Express was extended beyond Agra in 2018 — now Hazrat Nizamuddin–Virangana Lakshmibai Jhansi via Agra (general knowledge, not checked)
The Gatimaan Express (April 2016, 160 km/h) was launched between Delhi (Hazrat Nizamuddin) and Agra Cantt (now runs on to Jhansi).

s: Which is the fastest train in India?
o: Gatiman Express from Delhi to Agra
Satabdi Express from Delhi to Bhopal
Rajdhani Express from Delhi to Kolkata
Tejas Express from Mumbai to Goa
src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
x:
since 2019 Vande Bharat trains also run at 160 km/h (design 180 km/h) — now Vande Bharat is usually named India's fastest train (general knowledge, not checked)
In 2017 the Gatimaan Express (Delhi–Agra, 160 km/h) was India's fastest train (now Vande Bharat runs at the same speed); Shatabdi, Rajdhani and Tejas were slower.
flag: Outdated: Vande Bharat now also runs at 160 km/h and is usually called fastest.

s: The National Rail and Transportation Institute (NRTI) is situated in
x:
NRTI was upgraded in 2022 — now Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya, Vadodara (general knowledge, not checked)
The National Rail and Transportation Institute was set up at Vadodara (now Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya).

s:
Which of the following State Capitals of North-East India is/are connected by Indian Railways?

I. Imphal
II. Agartala

III. Kohima
IV. Aizawl
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x:
Aizawl joined the rail network on 13 Sep 2025 (Bairabi–Sairang line) — now Agartala, Itanagar (Naharlagun) and Aizawl are rail-connected (web search: newsonair.gov.in, 13 Sep 2025)
In 2015 only Agartala among these capitals had a rail link (now Aizawl too, via Sairang, since Sep 2025); Imphal and Kohima are still not connected.

s: The longest railway platform in India is
x:
Gorakhpur (1,366 m) held the record when asked — now Shree Hubballi Siddharoodha Swamiji station, Karnataka (1,507 m, 2023) has the longest platform (app notes 4:92)
Gorakhpur had the longest platform in 2012 (now Hubballi, 1,507 m).

s: What is the approximate track length of South Central Railway (choose nearest figure)?
src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
x:
South Coast Railway (1 Jun 2026) took the AP divisions — now South Central Railway has only the Secunderabad, Hyderabad and Nanded divisions (app notes 4:92)
When asked, South Central Railway had about 6,000 km of route (now smaller, after the AP divisions moved to South Coast Railway in June 2026).
flag: Outdated: AP divisions moved to South Coast Railway (June 2026), SCR now smaller.

s: Which is the longest National Highway of India?
x:
NHs were renumbered in 2010 — now NH-44 (Srinagar–Kanyakumari) is the longest (NextGen Indian Geography APPSC 11 p.3)
In the old numbering NH-7 (Varanasi–Kanyakumari) was the longest National Highway (now NH-44 after the 2010 renumbering).

s: As per Central Organization for Railway Electrification, India, till 1 March 2024, how much of total broad-gauge railway network has electrified?
src: APPSC 2023 Screening test (Online Mode) to the post of Deput
x:
electrification has advanced — now 99.6% of the broad-gauge network (23 May 2026; app notes 4:92)
CORE put broad-gauge electrification at about 94% on 1 March 2024 (now 99.6%, May 2026).
flag: Outdated now (99.6%, May 2026); key valid for date asked.

s: The second longest national waterway in India is
x:
NW-4 was extended by the National Waterways Act 2016 — now 2,890 km, longer than NW-1 (1,620 km) (PMF Human & Economic Geography 02 p32)
The Buckingham Canal is part of National Waterway-4 (Kakinada-Puducherry canals with the Godavari and Krishna), which at 1,095 km was the second longest NW after NW-1 (1,620 km); Jawahar, Sharda and Sutlej-Yamuna link are irrigation canals, not national waterways (now NW-4 is 2,890 km after the 2016 Act).

s:
Consider the following statements.

I. Currently three waterways have been declared as the National Waterways of India.

II. The Sadiya-Dhubri stretch of river Brahmaputra is the longest National Waterway.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x:
only 3 NWs in 2008 — now 111 NWs under the National Waterways Act 2016, so today neither statement is correct (PMF Human & Economic Geography 02 p31)
In 2008 (before NW-4 and NW-5 were declared at the end of 2008) only three National Waterways existed, so statement I was correct; statement II is wrong because NW-1 Allahabad-Haldia (1,620 km) is longer than NW-2 Sadiya-Dhubri (891 km). (Now 111 NWs, so statement I is no longer true.)

s: In all, how many international airports are there in India?
x:
16 international airports at exam time — now 33 international airports out of 149 operational (2023) (PMF Human & Economic Geography 02 p36)
In the early 2000s India was reported to have 16 international airports, the printed key (now 33 international airports out of 149 operational, 2023).
flag: Outdated: now ~33 international airports (2023).

s: Which of the following is not included in Edgar Dale's Cone of Experience?
src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II (Male & Female) in AP
x: Dale's original Cone of Experience (1946) had a band 'radio, recordings, still pictures' but no television; television was added only in the 1954 edition. Verbal symbols, visual symbols and radio are all in the cone, so television is the best answer.
flag: Later editions (1954) include television; key rests on 1946 version. | Original 1946 Cone had radio/recordings/still pictures; television added in 1954.

s:

Telecom Network - Rank

III. 4

d. BSNL -
IV. 2

subscriber ranking changed — now Jio 1, Airtel 2, Vodafone Idea 3, BSNL 4 (TRAI monthly subscription data)
In early 2019 (exam time) Vodafone Idea had the most subscribers, then Airtel, Jio and BSNL; Jio became No. 1 from mid-2019 (now Jio, Airtel, Vi, BSNL). Moved.

s: Which of the following is the deep water port of Andhra Pradesh?
src: APPSC 2018 Lecturers in Government Polytechnic Colleges (Eng
x: Gangavaram (near Visakhapatnam) is a greenfield deep-water port with the deepest draft in India; Ravva is a captive oil port and Meghavaram and Narsapur are only proposed.
flag: | Meghavaram is only proposed.; Narsapur is only proposed.

s: How many National Highways does the state of Andhra Pradesh have?
src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
x:
the State now has 55 National Highways covering 8,744 km (AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 p146)
38 was the count of National Highways in AP given in the 2022 paper (printed key); the Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 now lists 55 NHs (8,744 km).

s: In Andhra Pradesh the road length maintained by the Roads and Buildings Ministry of March 2006 is
x:
undivided-AP figure of 2006 — now 45,379 km of R&B roads + 8,744 km of NHs in the residual State (AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 p143)
63,639 km is the R&B road length of the then (undivided) Andhra Pradesh in March 2006 (printed key); today the residual State's R&B network is 45,379 km plus 8,744 km of NHs.
flag: Undivided-AP figure; residual State's R&B network is now 45,379 km.

s: In which district of Andhra Pradesh, is the proposed port at Dugarajapatnam located?
x:
Vakadu mandal moved out of SPSR Nellore in the April 2022 district reorganisation — now Tirupati district (CARE APPSC CA Sep 2026 p27)
Dugarajapatnam (Vakadu mandal) was in SPSR Nellore district when this was asked (2019); it was never in Chittoor, Krishna or Prakasam (now Tirupati district, since the April 2022 reorganisation).

s: What is the approximate total length of the coastal line of India, including Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands?
src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer, Assistant Public Relation
x:
the coastline was officially recounted in 2025 — now 11,098.81 km including islands (PIB Release 2198800, 4 Dec 2025)
The figure long given was about 7,517 km (7,516.6 km) including the islands (now 11,098.81 km after the 2025 recount, PIB Dec 2025).

s: Which of the following cities is not included in the Tentative list of UNESCO World heritage sites?
src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
x:
Ahmedabad (2017) and Jaipur (2019) have left the Tentative List — now inscribed World Heritage Sites (PMF Art & Culture 06 p.74-75)
Tirupati has never been on India's UNESCO Tentative List; Delhi, Ahmedabad and Jaipur city nominations were (Ahmedabad and Jaipur have since been inscribed, 2017 and 2019).

s: How many UNESCO World Heritage Sites does India have as on July 2025?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
x:
44 in July 2025 — now 45 after Sarnath was inscribed in July 2026 (48th session, Busan) (Rocket CA 2026-02 p.164)
With the Maratha Military Landscapes (July 2025, 47th session, Paris) India had 44 World Heritage Sites in July 2025 (now 45 with Sarnath, July 2026).
flag: Now 45 with Sarnath (July 2026).

s: In which of the following States, the tourist center Leh is situated?
src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
x:
Leh was in Jammu & Kashmir — now in the Union Territory of Ladakh (J&K Reorganisation Act 2019, from 31 Oct 2019) (general knowledge, not checked)
Leh was in the State of Jammu & Kashmir when asked (now in the Union Territory of Ladakh, since 31 October 2019).

s:
Consider the following statements about 'Tirupati'-

a. Tirupati is located at 13.65°N 79.42°E in the Chittoor District of Andhra Pradesh.

b. The city is also referred to as the 'Spiritual Capital of Andhra Pradesh'.

c. For the year 2012-13, India's Ministry of Tourism named Tirupati as the 'Best Heritage City'.
Which of the statements are correct?
src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
x:
Tirupati was in Chittoor district — now headquarters of Tirupati district (formed 4 April 2022) (general knowledge, not checked)
All three are correct: Tirupati lies at about 13.65°N 79.42°E, is called the Spiritual Capital of AP, and the Ministry of Tourism named it 'Best Heritage City' for 2012-13 (award given 18 Feb 2014). It was in Chittoor district then (now Tirupati district).

s: Ahobilam is situated in which district?
x:
Ahobilam was in Kurnool district — now in Nandyal district (formed April 2022) (AP Socio-Economic Survey 2024-25 p.169)
Ahobilam, with the nine Narasimha shrines in the Nallamala, was in Kurnool district (now Nandyal district).
flag: Now in Nandyal district (April 2022).

s:
Consider the following statements about 'Belum Caves':

a. The Belum Caves are located in Kolimigundla Mandal of Kurnool District in the state of Andhra Pradesh.

b. The first records of the Belum Caves come from the expedition report of British geologist and archaeologist Robert Bruce Foote, in 1884.
Which of the above statement/s is/are correct?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
x:
Kolimigundla mandal was in Kurnool district — now in Nandyal district (formed April 2022) (CDI AP History G2 PYQs: Belum Caves in Nandyal district)
Both are correct: Belum Caves are in Kolimigundla mandal (then Kurnool, now Nandyal district) and were first recorded by Robert Bruce Foote in 1884.

s: Lambasingi is known as the 'Kashmir of Andhra Pradesh'. Under which district does it fall?
x:
Lambasingi was in Visakhapatnam district — now in Alluri Sitharama Raju district (formed April 2022) (app notes 4:98)
Lambasingi, the 'Kashmir of AP', was in Visakhapatnam district (Chintapalli mandal), now Alluri Sitharama Raju district.
flag: Now in Alluri Sitharama Raju district.

s: The correct sequence of energy sources in order of their share in the power sector in India is :
x:
wind passed nuclear by 2014 and solar and wind have since passed hydro — now Thermal > Solar > Wind > Hydro > Nuclear by capacity (app notes 4:99, Aug 2026 data)
Thermal leads, then hydro; of the orders offered only Thermal > Hydro > Nuclear > Wind keeps thermal and hydro on top (now: Thermal > Solar > Wind > Hydro > Nuclear).

s: Which one of the following states of India ranks first in installed capacity and generation of electricity?
x:
in 2006 Maharashtra led in installed capacity and generation — now Gujarat is first (app notes 4:99, Dec 2025)
Gujarat is now first in gross installed capacity (Dec 2025) (in 2006 Maharashtra was first).

s: Ramagundam Super Thermal Power Station is located in–
x:
Telangana was carved out of Andhra Pradesh on 2 June 2014 — now Ramagundam is in Telangana (AP Reorganisation Act 2014)
NTPC's Ramagundam STPS (2,600 MW) is in Peddapalli district, which was in Andhra Pradesh when asked (now Telangana).

s:
Arrange the following states in descending order of coal production and choose the correct answer using codes given below.

I. Chhattisgarh
II. Jharkhand

III. Madhya Pradesh
IV. Odisha
Codes
x:
the ranking has changed — now (2020-21) Chhattisgarh 157.7 MT > Odisha 143 > Jharkhand 131.7 > MP 125.7 (PMF Human & Economic Geography 03 p.22)
In 2008 Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh led coal output, then Odisha, with Madhya Pradesh last (now Chhattisgarh and Odisha lead).

s: Which state in India produces the largest amount of coal ?
x: Of the options Orissa (Odisha) was the largest coal producer (Talcher, Ib valley), ahead of Madhya Pradesh; West Bengal's output is small and Bihar's coalfields went to Jharkhand in 2000.
flag: Answer depends on year; Jharkhand/Chhattisgarh/Odisha alternate as No.1 and none of the first two is offered. | Bihar's coalfields went to Jharkhand in 2000.

s: As of April 2025, which of the following power projects in Andhra Pradesh is the largest thermal power station by capacity?
o: Dr. Narla Tata Rao Thermal Power Station
src: APPSC 2023 Lecturers in Government Degree Colleges
x: Dr Narla Tata Rao TPS (2,560 MW, after its 800 MW unit) is AP's largest thermal station, ahead of Sri Damodaram Sanjeevaiah TPS, Krishnapatnam (2,400 MW), Simhadri (2,000 MW) and Rayalaseema (1,050 MW).
flag: Rayalaseema capacity in explanation (1,050 MW) is outdated; ranking unchanged.

s: Which one of the following states is a leading producer of Solar energy in India?
x:
Karnataka led installed solar capacity till 2021 — now Rajasthan is 1st in installed solar (pv-magazine India, Sep 2021; MNRE state-wise data)
In 2020 Karnataka (Pavagada park) had the largest installed solar capacity, about 7.4 GW, ahead of Rajasthan (5.2 GW) (now Rajasthan leads, since Sept 2021).

s: The correct sequence in descending order of the given countries in terms of railway length in the world is
x:
Official key: USA, Canada, India, Germany (older data). Strictly now: USA, India, Canada, Germany (Rocket World Geography #17 p.27).
older data ranked Canada above India — now USA > India > Canada > Germany (Rocket World Geography #17 p.27; Wikipedia list of countries by rail network size)
The UPPSC key is USA, Canada, India, Germany (option 3), from older data that put Canada's network ahead of India's. Current figures are USA (~220,000 km) > India (~69,000-70,000 km) > Canada (~49,000 km) > Germany (~33,000-39,800 km), an order no option shows (now USA > India > Canada > Germany).

s: What is the rank of Andhra Pradesh in terms of length of coast line amongst the coastal states of India?
x:
the old count gave AP 974 km and 2nd place (printed key 'Second') — now 3rd with 1,053.07 km after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu 1,068.69 km (PIB Release 2198800, 4 Dec 2025)
In the revised coastline count (India 11,098.81 km) Andhra Pradesh has 1,053.07 km and ranks third, after Gujarat (2,340.62 km) and Tamil Nadu (1,068.69 km) (now 3rd; it was '2nd, 974 km' when this 2023 paper was set).
flag: Printed key at exam time was 'Second' (974 km, old count); the data key 'Third' follows the Dec 2025 PIB revision. | AP was 2nd (974 km) in the old count; now 3rd after Gujarat and TN.

s: The world's highest ground-based telescopic observatory is located at :
x:
Hanle (India) is no longer the highest — now the University of Tokyo Atacama Observatory (TAO), Cerro Chajnantor, Chile, 5,640 m, opened 1 May 2024 (physicsworld.com)
In 2002 the Indian Astronomical Observatory at Hanle, Ladakh (about 4,500 m) was billed as the world's highest ground-based optical telescope site, so India was the answer then (now the University of Tokyo Atacama Observatory, Chile, 5,640 m, opened May 2024, is the highest).

s: Which of the following waves are used by the common TV remote control?
src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
x: TV remote controls use infrared waves (an IR LED).
flag: | Ultrasonic remotes are obsolete; common remotes use infrared.

s:
Consider the following statements.

I. According to the Indian Patents Act, a biological process to create seed can be patented in India.

II. In India, there is no Intellectual Property Appellate Board.

III. Plant varieties are not eligible to be patented in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x:
IPAB was abolished in April 2021 (Tribunals Reforms Ordinance/Act 2021) — now 'there is no IPAB' is true, so today II and III would be correct (general knowledge, not checked)
Only III was correct in 2019: plant varieties are not patentable (protected under the PPV&FR Act 2001), and essentially biological processes for producing seeds are excluded (Sec. 3(j)), so I is wrong; II was wrong then because IPAB existed (since 2003) (now IPAB is abolished, so II would also be true).

s: Where is the India's permanent research station Dakshin Gangotri?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer (Mains) Paper-I General Studies
x: Dakshin Gangotri was India's first research station in Antarctica (1983-84), not in the Himalayas or a sea.
flag: Stem says 'permanent'; it is now only a supply base.

s: The present Director General of ICAR, New Delhi, is :
x:
ICAR's Director General has changed — now Dr Mangi Lal Jat (Secretary DARE and DG ICAR) (Praveen CA360 Jan 2026 p.36; Daily CA 2 Nov 2026 p.3)
When asked (2015), Dr S. Ayyappan was Secretary DARE and DG, ICAR (now Dr M.L. Jat). Paroda, Mangala Rai and Chopra were earlier heads.

s: E-PG Pathshala is hosted at
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
x:
printed answer 'INFLIBNET, Ahmedabad' — now INFLIBNET Centre, Infocity, Gandhinagar (Wikipedia INFLIBNET Centre).
e-PG Pathshala (MoE/UGC portal of PG e-content) is hosted by the INFLIBNET Centre, which is now at Gandhinagar, Gujarat (formerly Ahmedabad).

s: Where is the headquarters of Andhra Pradesh Innovative Society located?
src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
x:
APIS started at Rushikonda, Visakhapatnam — now its office is at Mangalagiri, Amaravati region (startupgrantsindia.com listing)

flag: Office now at Mangalagiri, so Amaravati could be argued today; key is exam-time fact. | At exam time HQ was Visakhapatnam; office has since moved to Mangalagiri (Amaravati region).

s: Who is the only scientist in the world to have won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry twice?
x:
'only scientist to win the Chemistry Nobel twice' — now K. Barry Sharpless also has two (2001, 2022) (general knowledge, not checked)
When asked (2020) Frederick Sanger (1958, 1980) was the only double Chemistry laureate; now K. Barry Sharpless (2001, 2022) has also won twice. Marie Curie won Physics and Chemistry.

s: Who among the following is the only woman to win the Nobel Prize in Economics?

s: The latest Android mobile operating system-6.0 is named as :

Android 6.0 Marshmallow (2015) is no longer the latest — now Android 17 (stable 16 June 2026) (androidauthority.com/android-17-release-date-3639790)
Android 6.0 is Marshmallow (2015); Lollipop is 5.x, KitKat 4.4, Jelly Bean 4.1-4.3 (now the latest is Android 17, June 2026).

s: Which of the following is NOT correct about supercomputers?
o: India's Supercomputer Programme was started in late 1980s
Pratyush Supercomputer is established at Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology
PARAM 8000 is considered to be India's first supercomputer
United States of America is number one with maximum number of supercomputers

s: The latest edition of Bluetooth is
src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
x:
Bluetooth moved on to 5.2-5.4, 6.0 (2024, Channel Sounding), 6.1 (May 2025), 6.2 (Nov 2025) and 6.3 (May 2026) – now Bluetooth Core 7.0 (Nov 2026, High Data Throughput) (bluetooth.com blog 6 May 2026; audioxpress.com 4 Nov 2026).
When the paper was set (2019), Bluetooth 5.1 was the latest version (now Bluetooth Core 7.0, adopted Nov 2026).

s: The agency for the measurement for TV audiences is
x: BARC (Broadcast Audience Research Council, 2015) measures TV audiences in India; it replaced TAM ratings. IRS and NRS are readership surveys.
flag: TAM did measure TV audiences before BARC; correct only as current fact. | TAM was replaced by BARC (2015) as India's TV rating agency.
